answer: Marble Lagoon Filter Agents must maintain continuous attention on a shared lagoon of real-time data streams. Each identity is assigned a unique marble that shifts position only when actively observed. Falling below minimum observation frequency causes the marble to sink toward the lagoon’s nadir, triggering suspension. An attacker creating many identities must sustain attention across all marbles simultaneously. The cost is linear in identity count: each fake agent demands full attention bandwidth, which cannot be split without risk of detection.
